This is Richard Cowan reporting with the 4:20 Marijuana Headline News. 

As I was saying, when I was so rudely interrupted almost twenty years ago in beautiful downtown Vancouver, Canada: It’s 4:20. Do you know where your freedom is? 

Oh, you think it’s somewhere safe? Well, I would not be so sure.

The reason that I decided to bring back MarijuanaNews.com and start doing the 4:20 Marijuana Headline News (something that started in 2000 with Marc Emery and Pot TV — and would eventually be called a “Podcast” — is simply that I am feeling Deja Vu all over again.

Yes, of course, recreational marijuana is more or less legal in 24 states, and medical marijuana is more or less legal in 38 states, but do the math and read the fine print. But what could possibly go wrong? 

Back in the early 1990s, when I was still the National Director of NORML , I started saying that the best two word explanation for marijuana prohibition is bad journalism. Well, it still is.

Now for a great quote: the Spanish American historian George Santiana said that “Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.”

But, I like to say that marijuana prohibition causes long term memory loss, and what if those who cannot remember the past are what Paul Weaver called the “Editocracy”? 

Also see Why the News Is Not the Truth by Peter Vanderwicken

Then we are the ones who will have to repeat it. And it isn’t just the past. Do the math: There are still 26 states where recreational marijuana is illegal and twenty two states that don’t have any form of medical exemptions. 

Oh, and there are still over 200,000 arrests every year for simple possession of marijuana. 

See Long-Term Mental Health Consequences of Being Arrested on Arrestees and Their Families

And speaking of DEI, not DEA, non-whites are getting more than their fair share of being arrested. Just like the good old days. Ah, yes.

But what really “triggered” me (Don’t trigger me) were a series of articles in National Geographic, and Newsweek, and even in The Atlantic, one of the finest magazines in the world, with the shocking, shocking revelation that  Marijuana Is Too Strong Now “As weed has become easier to obtain, ihas become harder to smoke.”  

Well, let’s get something out of the way. Yes, the average THC percentage in marijuana has been increasing for the last 58 years, since I first got high in 1967. But people did get high in 1967, and as some wag said, the sixties were not about a placebo. But there are several problems with the Prohibitionist party line. First, as I said, yes, I am confident that THC levels have been going up since the 1960s, but remember THC wasn’t discovered until 1964 in Israel and widespread testing did get started until years later. Second, the accuracy of testing contraband depends on how representative the samples are. And we had no idea what was really in the baggies. We didn’t know about THC, or CBD, or any of the other Cannabinoids, or the terpenoids. (Or the herbicides that Nixon got Mexico to spray on the fields, to protect the children, of course.) The point is very simple. There has never been a standard dose of anything about contraband anything, especially including marijuana.

So, what did we do? And what is the difference between 5% THC and 15% THC? Allow me to illustrate.One is 5% Two is 10% Three is 15%. And it comes in different sizes! Big ones called Spliffs, from Jamaica, mon! The more or less standard size called joints, skinny ones called pinners. In California, little ones are popular now, because the weed is so good. Oh, excuse me, deadly! What would we do if the Prohibitionists didn’t save us from ourselves!?

Meanwhile, when you go to a “package store”, where they sell prepackaged beverages with alcohol percentages ranging from about 5 percent for wine coolers to 95% for Everclear ethanol, you know exactly what you are getting.  Similarly, when you go into a place called a “bar”, you can get a variety of beverages with a wide range of alcohol content, depending on how much you tip the bartender. Small classes for Shots. Big glasses for wine, maybe a nice Chianti. As it happens, too much ethanol can be deadly, but there is no lethal level to cannabis. So, what is really key? That you know what you’re getting, and that is only possible when cannabis is legal, but you can still do what we did back in the olden days. Try it. You’ll like it. 

But then there is what they call the latest research that scientists want you to know. Stop the presses!  Really? 

From 1999 MarijuanaNews.com archives: Minneapolis Prohibitionist Opposes Hemp Cultivation, Says "The marijuana smoked at Woodstock contained "industrial hemp" levels of THC." The latest research is really just the oldest party line. 

See From 23 Years Ago Today: US Prohibitionist Threatens To Invade Canada Because of BC Bud and Medical Cannabis BC BUD was supposedly so strong that it was traded pound for pound for cocaine in Hollywood.

To quote the late, great James Thurber: “Ashes to ashes, and clay to clay, if the enemy doesn't get you your own folks may.”

This has been Richard Cowan with the 420 marijuana headline News. Sorry about the twenty years. See you again soon.
